trade.text: Released a report criticizing President Trump’s tariff taxes for raising costs for families.
trade.quote: detailing how President Trump's tariff taxes, his war with Iran, and his so-called "Big Beautiful Bill" are driving up costs

schools.text: Voted for a funding bill that temporarily blocked efforts to strip federal funding from schools.
schools.quote: this bill does not include a backdoor to fund Border Patrol. It also temporarily blocks the White House Office of Management and Budget’s push to strip federal funding from schools and hospitals

safety.text: Secured federal funding for Santa Ana College’s criminal justice academies to train correctional and peace officers.
safety.quote: $1,031,000 in FY26 for the college’s Criminal Justice Academies to enhance regional training programs and facilities to meet the current and future demand for correctional and peace officers.

immigration.text: Introduced legislation to create optional expedited processing for employment-based permanent labor certifications used in green-card applications.
immigration.quote: This bill gives the Department of Labor the resources to modernize the PERM process, reduce delays, and make sure our system works for employers, workers, and America's economy.

health.text: Released a report warning that cuts to Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act could cause people to lose coverage and raise premiums.
health.quote: An estimated 54,370 people in CA-46 are at risk of losing health coverage because of Trump's cuts to Medicaid and the ACA, and 27,000 more are paying higher premiums after Trump allowed enhanced ACA tax credits to expire.

voting.text: Voted against a resolution supporting the SAVE America Act and said it would create barriers to voter registration and voting.
voting.quote: I won’t vote for any bill that makes it harder for the people who defend this country to exercise their right to vote.

tax.text: Pan proposes reducing government spending and the size of government in order to reduce taxes.
tax.quote: My first priorities are to reduce the size and scope of government in order to reduce taxes.

wages.text: Pan says minimum-wage increases reduce jobs and supports raising worker pay through lower taxes instead.
wages.quote: We need to support free markets. Laws that keep prices down usually have unintended consequences.

trade.text: Pan supports targeted tariffs against unfair foreign subsidies but opposes blanket tariffs.
trade.quote: It is appropriate to apply tariffs when other countries unfairly subsidize their own industries

debt.text: Pan proposes reducing national debt while preserving existing Social Security and Medicare benefits for older people and changing the system for younger people.
debt.quote: It will guarantee current benefit levels for all retirees as well as anyone age 37 and over by changing the system for those under 37.

schools.text: Pan supports charter schools and vouchers to give parents more educational options.
schools.quote: I support school choice, which would allow parents to move their children to the best schools to meet their children’s needs.

safety.text: Pan says police should receive the resources and legal support needed to protect people and property and that laws should be enforced.
safety.quote: I will work to ensure our police officers have the resources and legal support they need to protect our lives and property.

immigration.text: Pan says public safety requires enforcing laws and maintaining secure borders while describing opportunities for immigrants.
immigration.quote: Pan is running to ensure public safety, maintain secure borders, empower school parents, transform welfare, and reduce the size and scope of government .

health.text: Pan proposes replacing much of the existing entitlement system with a health-insurance voucher used on the private market.
health.quote: The money would consist of $1000 per month as a direct deposit into each individual’s bank account and $4000 per year as a health insurance voucher to be used on the private market.
